description:
Accounts in the hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Neatly written, large, and detailed. Evidently he wrote much more neatly when submitting accounts to his partners as compared to his notes for himself. 

Headed: "explanation of the account of my master Abū l-Faḍl [...]." Mentions transactions in labdanum(?); cinnamon; lac; clove; red sandalwood; cardamom; Ibn Nuṣayr and Ibn ʿAzrūn; Socotran aloe; white sandalwood; the hire for a ship with Abū Saʿīd; someting "whose explanation is in another place." On verso, "and this is the explanation of the sale of the first merchandise," followed by a table of ~8 distinct items of clothing and how much they sold for. A few entries below refers to "the second" (set of merchandise) and itemizes it.
